system.summary: System A′: a homophonic substitution on graphic signs and numerals (↓ ω π 4 8 ÿ …), no word division, look-alike signs and per-hand variants, word signs for F.G. (Dominationes in Latin) and K (King Ferdinand), pair signs (Ro = und, 4#o = auch). The same system as R9368 and R9407 (augurelio1535); keys re-learned per letter.

diacritics.note: dots and rings split look-alikes (dotted ÿ = t, undotted γ = r; closed 4 = e, open ч = i)

system.sibling_key: R9407 (augurelio1535 pass 2 key) carried over by sign shape; R9368 gloss key tried on R9410 (failed)
system.notes: Measured distinct signs per letter 62-89 (sysA2/*_signs.txt), including look-alike and transcription variants.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear gloss over R9427 lines 1-10 and a few letters on R9410; no edition found (web search 2026-09-21).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied; problem posed with /goal; the user asked for a period German model. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Web search for KAA 4591 and Augurelio ciphers
DECODE record list from the API dump (141 records in the volume); images of the 14 targets and 30 neighbouring keys fetched with the cookie
Key from the R9368 gloss applied to R9410
R9427 gloss aligned: 'ewr F.G.' anchors the R9409/R9410 system; pinned annealing on R9410 and R9409
Full-zoom alignment of the R9427 gloss gave the System A' key; R9410 and R9409 read in part
R9408 (1534, ~7,300 signs) transcribed and read in part with the System A' key
Annealing with nulls allowed on R9410 (System A′): failed

R9408 look-alike split finished at the image: P6 l.24-31, P7 and six flagged tall looped signs on P5-P6 (all K, a seventh K at P6 l.10; two # -> U; three ringless δ b -> d; one dropped 8); 17 edits, r9408/transcription_v3.txt, r9408/split_p6p7.md. The R9410 split had already been applied to R9409, R9413 and R9427 (their split.md) but not recorded in NOTES.

Lexical measure sysA2/lexmeasure.py (DTA words + chancery vocabulary, Viterbi segmentation) calibrated on R9407: hand reading 0.912, pass-2 machine decrypt 0.786, the same under a random letter key 0.194. Old decrypts of the five A′ letters: R9408 0.585, R9409 0.582, R9410 0.690, R9413 0.647, R9427 0.546.

Improved R9407 key (augurelio1535/pass2/key.txt, polyphonic options) applied as is by sign shape to R9408, R9409 (codes mapped), R9410, R9413, R9427 with a word-aware beam: lexical share 0.661, 0.746, 0.785, 0.721, 0.633.

Per-letter key re-learned: Baum-Welch on a letter-trigram HMM (de-1500s) seeded with the R9407 key, Dirichlet prior to the seed, then word-beam decode and 4 rounds of re-estimation from the beam output (sysA2/run.py); merges c# = ck (R9408), w3v before F.G. = eur. Lexical share R9408 0.875, R9409 0.840, R9410 0.864, R9413 0.848, R9427 0.847. A pooled key over all five letters did no better than per-letter keys; LAM 1.0 slightly better than 0.6.

Per-letter keys show new merged look-alikes not split on the images: R9408 y = t and r (undotted γ coded y), R9408/R9427 4 = e and i (4 vs open ч as on R9407), R9409 ç+ = f/v, sch, da; R9413 Z mostly i, also u and e.

Hand reading rounds over every line of the five letters (r94xx/reading.txt; drafted by text-only reading agents from the decrypts with sysA2/show.py and checked with the strict sign-alignment measure sysA2/measure2.py; R9409 P7 read in the main session after the agent stopped). Words read (count.py, {?} unread): R9408 1358/1528 = 88.9%, R9409 1911/2361 = 80.9%, R9410 f.244r 255/304 = 83.9%, R9413 1431/1663 = 86.0%, R9427 419/542 = 77.3%; all five 5374/6398 = 84.0%. Strict measure2: 0.814, 0.721, 0.729, 0.799, 0.638.

Values forced by context in the readings: R9409 Ŧ = l, ç = s, ç+ = f/v, 7o/ço = h, ð = ich, Θ = n, ʝ = und; R9408 my = m, R = und, d = r; R9413 k = ich, d = r, Mj = m, ro = h, J+ = sch; R9427 R = und, nn = w, β = sch/f; all: Q = l/ll besides g, a lone β and a# are nulls. R9408 is signed Weinmaister, Ofen 8 Feb 1534; R9413 addressed to secretary Waisenfelder.
Supervised re-key from the hand readings (sysA2/supkey.py) and re-decode: lexical share fell (R9408 0.838, R9410 0.847, R9413 0.838, R9427 0.817), so the EM keys stand.
R9410 ff.246-247 (P3-P6, a second letter dated Anno XXXIIII) found never transcribed; left open.
R9410 ff.246-247 (images P3, P4, P6; P5 = P4) transcribed by hand from crops: 65 lines, 2,342 signs (r9410/transcription_p3p6.txt). Gloss over P3 l.1 and the clear phrases show the letter is Latin.

R9410 German key (re-learned) carried to the Latin letter and re-learned on the la model (sysA2/run.py --lang la): running Latin at once; 4o sign = et (in before q), hourglass X = the Dominationes code after Vestre.

R9410 ff.246-247 read: 350/422 words = 82.9% (r9410/reading_p3p6.txt). King John (Zápolya) to the Dukes of Bavaria, Buda, last day of June 1534: thanks for letters and news of the Landgrave and the Duke of Württemberg; only a truce with the adversary, which his side breaks; an envoy back at Constantinople; the Turks; amicitia and fraternitas.

Look-alike merges checked at the images (sysA2/lookalike_check.md): R9408 y = dotted ÿ (t) vs undotted γ (r) plus an m+γ ligature; R9408 4 = closed 4 (e) vs open ч (i); R9409 c+ one shape for da/ch/f, sch a separate open-hook sign. All match the values the readings already gave.

Splits applied from the readings (sysA2/applysplit.py: R9408 380 signs, R9409 9) and regraded: strict measure R9408 0.814 -> 0.812, R9409 0.721 -> 0.724; machine decrypts 0.875 -> 0.870, 0.840 -> 0.842. No unread words opened.

Image re-transcription of every line holding an unread word: R9408 98 lines (143 sign edits, transcription_v4), R9413 99 lines then a close-zoom pass on 67 (v3, v4), R9409 181 lines (~356 edits, v3). An R9408 second pass stopped at 20/72 lines (usage limit).
sysA2/fill.py: unread spans located by wildcard alignment, decoded by a lexicon-only beam over sign values attested in the pooled hand readings (per-hand weighted), with second-occurrence checks.
K word sign = King Ferdinand from context (Hieronymus of Zara sent to the Turk; Hungarian lords holding with K at Pressburg; the Württemberg war against K). 4#o ligature = auch.
Image re-transcription: R9408 second pass finished (6 lines corrected), R9427 44 lines (~95 edits), R9410 f.244r 23 lines (16 edits).
Final reading rounds: R9413 no further gain (94.3%); R9427 84.3%, R9410 f.244r 86.1%, R9408 92.0%; overall 89.3% (6132/6827). Stopped: nothing further passes the acceptance rules; no letter at 95%.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 13910 tokens, 70 types, de-1500s order 4: reading -2.671 per letter; polyphonic: 13% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from kaa4591 (catalogue 161), whose fourteen records are letters in at least six systems: System A′ stays in kaa4591; Łaski's System B is kaa4591b; R9325 is fulda1576; R9367, R9416, R9424 and R9319 are r9367, r9416, r9424 and r9319; R9291 is a key fragment. This entry keeps the five System A′ records (six letters); its measures were already per letter and System A′ only (validation.tsv likewise).

validation.notes: polyphonic: 13% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The System A′ key was first rebuilt from the contemporary gloss over ten lines of R9427 ('ewr F.G.'), then improved on the sibling letter R9407 (augurelio1535) and re-learned on each letter by EM and a word-aware decoder (2 Oct 2026).
outcome.notes: System A′ only (split 15 Oct 2026). 5 Oct 2026: R9413 94.3%, R9408 92.0%, R9410 ff.246-247 (Latin, King John, Buda 30 June 1534) 88.9%, R9409 87.2%, R9410 f.244r 86.1%, R9427 84.3% of words (6,132 of 6,827 = 89.8% overall; the 89.3% given before 15 Oct 2026 was a slip of arithmetic); K = Ferdinand by context. No letter reaches the 95% bar.
